newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 12.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Tuesday:

- A huge cut in unemployment over the next two years is forecast in a new economic survey which predicts a major growth in job creation - RTE has banned advertising of alcopops because of "concern about their appeal to young people."
- SDLP leader John Hume is expected to announce his decision on whether he will run for the presidency when he returns from holiday in two weeks time.
- UK fund managers moving out of equities into bond and cash holdings -
- Pan Andean working on farm-out deal in Bolivia
- Dunnes appoints first director of personnel
- Ryanair lifts pre-tax 29 percent to 5.7 million in first quarter
- Clinton uses veto on budget and tax bills
- Crean boosts U.S. food arm with $7 million poultry deal
- Flu costs put Health Boards in the red
- Ryanair is flying high as profits go on soaring

IRISH TIMES - Former prime minister Albert Reynolds will soon begin a series of meetings with Fianna Fail parliamentary colleagues in his attempt to secure the party's nomination to contest the presidential election. - The minister for justice has signalled his intention to introduce legislation amending the Refugee Act passed by the last parliament but not yet implemented. - Brokers predict inflation rise as pound, sterling gap widens. - Tesco project to create 200 jobs in Banbridge. - United Airlines is to hire 200 staff for a new telephone reservations centre in Dublin. - New director on Board as Dunnes puts the family in a minority. - A new tendering competition for a National Conference Centre is to be held.
